solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make up for poor spell in tennis match?

parts.note: food or form that is off is poor, below standard
a tennis match is divided into spells of play called sets

explanation.surface: A tennis player compensates for a bad patch during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor spell' reads as one phrase meaning a slump; cryptically 'poor' and 'spell in tennis match' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance or compensate for it with a gain elsewhere.

clue.text: Odd person needing employment — social services know about it

parts.note: an odd or eccentric person is informally called a case
a plain synonym for a job

explanation.surface: An eccentric needing a job is someone the social services already have on file.
explanation.definitionFit: Casework is the work social workers do with individual clients, so it is what social services know about.

clue.text: GB pal? Oh no, ill-disposed to English!

definitions.text: GB pal? Oh no, ill-disposed to English!

indicators.note: letters badly disposed are put in a poor arrangement, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as printed, ignoring punctuation
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be a pal to Britain, being hostile to the English.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone who says no to being Britain's pal and is ill-disposed to the English.
explanation.definitionFit: An anglophobe is a person who dislikes or fears England and its people and culture.

clue.text: Here's piano — play something we've heard many times before!

definitions.text: something we've heard many times before

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
play as in freedom of movement, the slack in a rope or system

explanation.surface: A musician produces a piano and plays a tune everyone is tired of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about performing; here it is the noun meaning room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark repeated so often it has lost any force or freshness.

clue.text: Bird is one that's black on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is on top sits above, so those pieces are written before the word that follows

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a bird with a dark head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on top' puts one and black above the word is.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Author is yellow, then in good health

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow
a plain synonym for healthy

explanation.surface: A writer is first cowardly, then recovers his health.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow seems to mean cowardly; it is the heraldic colour. George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the English writer of Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm.

clue.text: Brought into market there's some strange monkey

indicators.note: something brought into a place ends up inside it

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: a strange version of the word is an odd, rearranged one

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An exotic animal is on sale at a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small tropical American monkey with a long tail and silky fur.

clue.text: Soft soap that gets wet in the bathroom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: smooth flattering or evasive talk

definitions.text: that gets wet in the bathroom
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small cloth for washing the face

explanation.surface: A bar of mild soap goes soggy beside the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' looks like a bathroom product, but it is the idiom for flattery; flannel is the British word for a facecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for evasive flattering talk, and also the British name for a washcloth.

clue.text: Animal's left leg, one getting trapped

indicators.note: a thing that gets trapped is caught inside something else

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for left
in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal's left hind limb has something caught in it.
explanation.walkthrough: One goes inside left plus leg, between L and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is the large tawny wild cat of Africa, a classic example of an animal.

clue.text: Country lake west of peninsula

indicators.note: in an across entry, west of means placed to the left, so it comes first

parts.note: the map abbreviation for lake
the Iberian peninsula holds Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A geographical note placing a nation's lake to the west of a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African republic founded by freed American slaves, with Monrovia its capital.

clue.text: Explains magician's tricks — no longer secret

parts.note: a magician casts spells
a secret that is out is now known

explanation.surface: Someone exposes how a conjuror's illusions are done, so they are secret no more.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell something out is to explain it clearly and in full detail, step by step.

clue.text: Energy of second eleven maybe

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for second
an eleven is a cricket or football side; maybe marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A sports report on how lively the reserve side was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' reads as a reserve team; the setter splits it into second and eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is used figuratively for energy or momentum, as in running out of steam.

clue.text: Soldiers having bad time, needing to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a plain synonym for bad
the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An army unit going through a rough patch must withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially a cavalry or artillery subdivision.

clue.text: Goes along casually, using various bits from tool set

indicators.note: taking various bits and putting them together suggests a jumbled order

parts.note: the letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A handyman ambles about, improvising with odd items from the toolbox.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is an informal British verb for driving or wandering in a leisurely unhurried way.

clue.text: Definitely not tight-fisted

parts.note: surface reading: very generous with money
setter's reading: a fist clenched tight is the opposite of a palm spread flat

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works both ways: generous, and literally with the hand unclenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-handed means generous and liberal with money, the opposite of a miser who keeps his fist closed.

clue.text: Oversupply a friend with salt in food?

parts.note: a glut is an excess supply
taken as written
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A host oversalts a friend's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Monosodium glutamate is a salt added to food as a flavour enhancer; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Monosodium glutamate, the sodium salt of glutamic acid, is a common flavour enhancer added to processed food.

clue.text: We'd neglect man, OK? Not OK — recognition called for!

indicators.note: letters that are not OK are wrong as they stand and need fixing by rearrangement

parts.note: the letters taken as printed, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone asks if ignoring a man is fine, and is told it is not: he deserves credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The OK is used twice: once as fodder and once inside the instruction that it is not OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Acknowledgement is the act of recognising someone's work or presence, giving them credit.

clue.text: European in a train wandering around America

indicators.note: around means one part encloses the other
a wandering course is not straight, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: the letters taken as printed, then rearranged
the United States, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A continental traveller on a train touring the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian is a native of Austria, a country in central Europe, so is a European.

clue.text: Like some food in the course of journey that's kept cold

indicators.note: something kept is held inside, so one piece lies within the other

parts.note: French phrase used in English for on the way
the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Food on a journey that is kept chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: En croute describes food baked wrapped in a pastry crust, such as beef Wellington.

clue.text: Snake here more than half coiling around

indicators.note: coiling around turns a stretch back on itself, and more than half limits that turn to the front portion

parts.note: being here is being present

explanation.surface: A snake in this spot is mostly coiled up.
explanation.walkthrough: Of PRESENT's seven letters, the first four, more than half, are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpent is a literary word for a snake, especially a large one.

clue.text: Snub an expert on how religion should be taught?

indicators.note: an expert on a subject is named with the subject first, as in history buff, so the subject comes first

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the British school subject
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: Someone who knows all about teaching religion gets brushed off.
explanation.walkthrough: An RE buff is an expert on religious education, so the wordplay is read as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is an abrupt refusal or rejection, a snub given to an approach or offer.

clue.text: Kicks overworked hirelings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kicks or chops at, as at an opponent's shins
second meaning: drudges hired to do dull work, especially writers

explanation.surface: Exhausted hired hands lash out with their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to kick at someone's shins in football, and hacks are drudges paid for tedious work.

clue.text: Discover former lover in seaside county

parts.note: to suss is informal British for to work out or discover
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into an old flame at a coastal resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is an English county on the south coast, home to seaside towns like Brighton.

clue.text: Filthy stuff that gets stomachs churning over

indicators.note: turning over flips something, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: tums is informal for stomachs

explanation.surface: Obscene material makes people feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent material, and also literally soot or dirty specks.

clue.text: Machine in box office covered in rubbish

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
the standard abbreviation for box office

explanation.surface: A ticket machine at a theatre is buried under litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine able to carry out complex actions automatically.

clue.text: You no longer will sit in magnificent house

indicators.note: the word sits inside the following phrase, spanning the gap

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A former occupant of a stately home is no longer there.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic singular form of you, no longer in everyday use.

clue.text: Note mum, so frightfully important

indicators.note: something done frightfully is done in a terrible mess, so the order is scrambled

parts.note: the letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A child is told to remember that mother's message is very significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentous means of great significance or consequence for the future.

clue.text: Insult a female needing self-confidence

parts.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation for female
front is boldness or nerve, as in having the front to do something

explanation.surface: A woman who lacks self-assurance is slighted.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate insult or slight that offends someone's dignity.

clue.text: A short time in that place where the war action is?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a plain synonym for that place
taken as written
time cut short to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A soldier spends a brief spell at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatre of war is the region where fighting takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the area where military operations happen, so it is where the action is.
